blocks.text: According to Nork (loc. cit.) "son of the nest", from the same as קן (?).

בהמות is identical with the שור הבר known from legend, which will one day have to fight a battle with the Liviatan; because of its eating up the mountain fodder it is also called (in the well-known poem אקדמות recited on Schebuoth, in the 75th verse): תור טור, or more fully: תור טור רמותא "bull of the high mountain."
On the family relationships of Tobias see my נפשות צדיקים p. 62.

Josephus too (Bello jud. Book 7, Chap. 15) describes a plant Βααρας [Baaras] which is difficult to grasp and uproot, which succeeds only by pouring menstrual blood over it, and G. Surenhusius (in his Mishnah translated into Latin and annotated) then supposes that Βάρυας [Baryas] was read for Βααρας [Baaras] and that בר נש was formed from the former; a strange opinion, which takes its place worthily beside the whole fable.
